sentences.text: The petitioners have filed these petitions U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.11.2019.

2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
 On 15.11.2019 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 was standing on the side of the road and petitioner in MVC No.7607/2019 was pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0760,
near Yadavanahalli, Gate on Bengaluru NH7 ,the rider of the said motor cycle ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over his vehicle and Sri.

2 dashed it to the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 and  SCCH4 4 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 pillion rider i.e., petitioner in MVC 7607/2019,
consequently both the petitioners sustained injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru where he admitted as an inpatient for one week.

This petitioner has sustained injuries such as Left Shaft Tibia Communited Grade II fracture and other multiple injuries and under went surgery of left leg wound debridement,
suturing and IM nailing tibia under spinal anesthesia on 16.11.2019 and post operative period was uneventful.
The petitioner was very hale and healthy prior to the accident.
This petitioner was working as Mechanic and he was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/.
Due to the permanent disability sustained in the accident the petitioner is no longer in a position to do his Mechanic work and now is idle without doing any work.

Bengaluru.

Post procedure 4 pint PCV transfused, 10 units FFP, 7 pint RDPS transfused.
Post operative period was uneventful.
The petitioner was very hale and healthy prior to the accident.
This petitioner was working as Mason and he was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/.
Due to the permanent disability sustained in the accident the petitioner is no longer in a position to do his mason work and now is idle without doing any work.
SCCH4 6 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019  The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence the petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/for each ,with interest.
3. After service of notices the respondent No.1 placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has entered appearance through its advocate and filed objection statement.

The respondent No.2 has filed statement of objection by admitting the issuance of Package policy to the motor cycle bearing No.OD22L760 and the liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, the respondent No.1 has willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess the valid and effective driving license to ride the Sri.Manivel.R vs Shashikanta Patra on 16 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99699905/
4 same as on the date of the accident.
The alleged accident  SCCH4 7 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 was not occurred in the manner as pleaded by the petitioner.
The petitioner in MVC.No.7606/19 was main architect for the accident who tried to cross the road where there is no provision for crossing the road by the pedestrians.
The petitioner in MVC. No.7607/19 guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and not wearing the safety helmet, as such he is not entitle for the compensation.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive, exorbitant and unreasonable.

Accordingly,
respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of rival contention, the following common issues have been framed in all the petitions:
 1.

Whether the petitioners proves  that, they were sustained injuries due  to actionable negligent riding of the  motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L  0760 by its rider, in RTA took place on  15.11.2019 at 8.30 p.m., near Yeda  vanahalli Gate, on BengaluruHosur  NH7?
 SCCH4 8 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019  2.

Whether the petitioners are enti  tled for compensation? If so, what  amount and from whom?
 3.

What Order or Award?
 5.

through him 11 documents are marked at Ex.P1 to11.

The petitioners in MVC No7607/2019 is examined as Sri.Manivel.R vs Shashikanta Patra on 16 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99699905/

Dr.S.A.Somashekara, is examined in both cases as PW.3 and 4 and got marked Ex.P17 to 20.
When the case was put for evidence of respondent, its advocate submitted no evidence on their behalf.
6. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.

To prove the claim petitions both the petitioners have filed their affidavit in lieu of their chief examination, which are considered as PW.1 and 2.

On the basis of the statement, the police have registered FIR against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0706 for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
On the date of the registration of FIR the police have visited the place of accident and drawn spot mahazar as per Ex.p3.
The damages caused to motor cycle bearing Reg.No. KA 51HF9369 and OD22L0760 are also noted in Ex.P.4 IMV report.

As pr the wound certificates and discharge summaries issued by Sparsh Hospital the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 took treatment from 15.11.2019 to 18.11.2019 and from 13.12.2019 to 14.12.2019 and petitioner in MVC.No.7607/19 took treatment on 16.11.2029.
 9.

The jurisdictional police, after conducting investigation have submitted charge sheet against one  SCCH4 11 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 Thapan Kumar who is the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KAOD22L0760 for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IMV Act.
The charge sheet is also marked under Ex.P.7.

In the charge sheet also it has been alleged on 15.11.2019, the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA51HF9369 and the petioner in Sri.Manivel.R vs Shashikanta Patra on 16 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99699905/
7 MVC.No.7607/2019 was pillion rider, while they coming from Bengaluru, near Yedavanahalli bus stop a phone call came to the mobile of petitioner Manivelu.

Hence order to receive the phone call the said petitioner stopped his vehicle on the left side of the road and receiving the phone call by that time, the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0760 came from Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the motor cycle wherein the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 was stopped on the left side of the road due to which, the petitioner sustained  SCCH4 12 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 injuries.
But the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 it has been stated the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L 0760 dashed while the petitioner was standing on the by the side of road.
However it is necessary to see that whether petitioner sustained injury or not.
10. The respondent No.1 is not contesting the petition.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement though denied the accident but its defence is that petitioner was main architect for the causing the alleged accident who tried to cross the road where there is no provision for crossing the road by the pedestrians.
Thus the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, he is not entitled to claim the compensation.

11. In the crossexamination of PW.1 and 2 Sri.Manivel.R vs Shashikanta Patra on 16 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99699905/
8 nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 did not entered the  SCCH4 13 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 witness box to adduce rebuttal evidence.
There are no materials to prove that, the petitioners are responsible for the accident.
12. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petitions like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
Though there is 4 days delay in lodging FIR , when the respondent contended that petitioner is an architecture of the accident some delay in lodging FIR is not an important thing.

13. Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that, they are sustained injuries in the accident dated 15.11.2019 which is caused by the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0760, by its rider.

Accordingly,
I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

The petitioners have filed these petitions U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.11.2019.

 On 15.11.2019 at about 8.30 p.m., the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 was standing on the side of the road and petitioner in MVC No.7607/2019 was pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0760,

SCCH4 6 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019  The respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the basis of the statement, the police have registered FIR against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0706 for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The jurisdictional police, after conducting investigation have submitted charge sheet against one  SCCH4 11 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 Thapan Kumar who is the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KAOD22L0760 for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IMV Act.
Hence order to receive the phone call the said petitioner stopped his vehicle on the left side of the road and receiving the phone call by that time, the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0760 came from Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the motor cycle wherein the petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 was stopped on the left side of the road due to which, the petitioner sustained  SCCH4 12 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 injuries.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement though denied the accident but its defence is that petitioner was main architect for the causing the alleged accident who tried to cross the road where there is no provision for crossing the road by the pedestrians.
Thus the petitioner being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, he is not entitled to claim the compensation.
The respondent No.2 did not entered the  SCCH4 13 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 witness box to adduce rebuttal evidence.
There are no materials to prove that, the petitioners are responsible for the accident.
12. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petitions like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
Though there is 4 days delay in lodging FIR , when the respondent contended that petitioner is an architecture of the accident some delay in lodging FIR is not an important thing.
13. Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that, they are sustained injuries in the accident dated 15.11.2019 which is caused by the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.OD22L0760, by its rider.
It is also not the case of respondent that, implant is removed.
Hence, it can be considered that the petitioner is required at least Rs.50,000/ for future medical expenses.
The petitioner has not produced any evident to prove his avocation and income.
In the decision reported in 2021 ACJ 1592 in the case Yashodha.H and others V/s Sharath Acharya and another the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka was please to award the compensation by taking notional income as fixed by the High Court Legal Service committee.
opennyai_summary.decision:
23 . Hence, I inclined to award the compensation to the petitioner under the following heads:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,68,800/
2. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 16,776/
 up period and attendant charge.
3. Conveyance charges Rs. 10,000/
4. Pain and sufferings Rs. 40,000/
Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.14,000/ X 12 X 18 X 24% =Rs.7,25,760/ which is the total loss of future income.
 SCCH4 24 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019  33.
Hence, I inclined to award the compensation to the petitioner under the following heads:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 7,25,760/
2. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 18,640/
 up period and attendant charge.
3. Conveyance charges Rs. 10,000/
4. Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/
5.
Food nourishment, attendant Rs. 10,000/
 charges and loss of amenities 6.
Medical bills Rs. 2,75,811/
7.
Hence the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2
SCCH4 25 MVC No.7606 and  7607/2019 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation Sri.
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petitions filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
SCCH4 26 MVC No.7606 and 7607/2019 The petitioner in MVC No.7606/2019 is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,77,696/ along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.
The petitioner in MVC No.7607/2019 is entitled for compensation of Rs.11,40,211/along with interest at the rate of 6% from the date of petition till realization of the amount.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of this order.
Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioners in both the cases, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through Epayment on their proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or SCCH4 27 MVC No.7606 and 7607/2019 Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in their names.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/ in both the petitions.
Draw an award accordingly in all the claim petitions.
